label: Refuted Aristotelian-scholastic claims of women's natural rational inferiority
description: In The Book of the City of Ladies (1405), Christine de Pizan systematically dismantled medieval Aristotelian and clerical authorities who portrayed women as defective males lacking full reason.
dialecticalTension: Uses Aristotelian logical demonstration against Aristotelian biological-gender prejudice.
historicalContext: Inaugurated the pan-European Querelle des Femmes in late medieval Paris.

citations.author: Christine de Pizan
citations.work: The Book of the City of Ladies

label: Modeled allegorical philosophical consolation and Lady Reason's dialogue
description: Christine explicitly modeled the opening despair and allegorical visitation of Lady Reason in Le Livre de la Cité des Dames and L'Avision Christine on Boethius's Consolation of Philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Transforms Boethian philosophical consolation from personal misfortune to collective gender justice.
historicalContext: Late medieval French humanism at the court of Charles VI.

citations.author: Karen Green
citations.work: The Woman of Reason: Feminism, Humanism and Political Thought

label: Prefigured autonomous women's scholarly communities and defense of female reason
description: Christine's allegorical City of Ladies—a fortress built by women's intellectual achievements—directly foreshadowed Mary Astell's Serious Proposal for a women's philosophical academy.
dialecticalTension: Links late medieval Querelle des Femmes to early modern feminist rationalism.
historicalContext: Continuity in European feminist philosophical defenses of education (1405–1694).

citations.author: Jacqueline Broad and Karen Green
citations.work: A History of Women's Political Thought in Europe, 1400–1700

label: Established the foundational argument that female inferiority is cultural, not natural
description: Christine de Pizan's argument that unequal education explains apparent intellectual differences anticipated Mary Wollstonecraft's Enlightenment Vindication by nearly four centuries.
dialecticalTension: Connects late-medieval feminist argumentation with Enlightenment political philosophy.
historicalContext: Longue durée of European feminist philosophy from 1405 to 1792.
